howToExport: Log in to americanexpress.com and open the card's statements and activity.
Pick a statement period or a custom date range and choose Download.
Select CSV as the format (additional transaction details, if offered, are ignored) and drop the file above.
knownQuirks: Amex lists charges as positive numbers and payments as negative, the opposite of what QuickBooks expects for a card upload, so purchases land as money received. The preset inverts every sign.
Extended Details and City/State are multi-line fields inside quotes; some spreadsheet tools split them into extra rows. The preset parses them correctly and leaves them out.
The Category column is Amex's own classification and isn't accepted by QuickBooks' 3-column import.
Dates are MM/DD/YYYY; QuickBooks companies outside the US need DD/MM/YYYY.

howToExport: Download the statement from your bank as CSV, Excel (.xls/.xlsx), .QBO, .OFX or .QIF: the tool reads all of them.
Drop it here and check the preview, the totals and the opening and closing balance check.
Type the exact names of the bank or card account and of the offset accounts, as they appear in your Chart of Accounts.
Download the 5-row test file first, import it into a backed-up company file, then download the full file.
knownQuirks: QuickBooks Desktop has no undo for .IIF imports, and any account name it doesn't recognise is created as a new account: type the names exactly as in your Chart of Accounts.
Each transaction is a TRNS line plus SPL lines that must add up to zero. The tool checks every transaction to the cent and refuses to create a file that doesn't balance.
Money out is written as CHECK and money in as DEPOSIT (CREDIT CARD and CCARD REFUND for card accounts), following Intuit's own sample files.
QuickBooks Desktop 2023 lost its connected services, including bank feeds, on 31 May 2026; .IIF import runs inside QuickBooks and keeps working.

howToExport: Sign in to online banking on a computer and open the account's transaction history.
Choose the date range: a full statement month is easiest to reconcile.
Choose Download or Export in CSV or Excel (.xlsx/.xls). If the bank offers QuickBooks (.QBO) itself, you can import that directly.
Drop the file here, compare the totals with your statement, then pick your bank in the .QBO settings.
knownQuirks: QuickBooks Desktop checks the file's Intuit bank ID (INTU.BID) against Intuit's list and stops at unknown banks. Pick yours from the list, which comes from Intuit's own Web Connect directory.
QuickBooks skips a transaction whose FITID it has already imported into the account. The tool gives the same transaction the same ID every time, and two identical charges on one day different IDs.
.QBO files are declared US-ASCII, so accents and symbols are folded to plain letters; payee names are cut to 32 characters and memos to 255.
Dates are written at noon GMT, so no time zone can move a transaction to the day before or after.

howToExport: In the IBKR Portal, open the reports area and choose Statements → Activity.
Pick the period (monthly, yearly or custom dates) and CSV as the format.
Run and download the statement, then drop it above; choose a section in the Section menu.
knownQuirks: Every row starts with its section name and Header or Data, so one CSV holds dozens of tables with different columns; Excel shows it as one jagged sheet.
Trades include SubTotal and Total rows plus ClosedLot detail rows under closing trades. Summing Proceeds without removing them double-counts; the preset drops all three.
Trade times are written as «2024-01-15, 10:30:01», with a comma inside the date, which Excel treats as text; the preset keeps the date only.
Numbers mix integers and decimals from row to row; they're written uniformly so Excel sums and pivots work.

howToExport: Open N26 in a web browser; the CSV download is offered in the web app.

knownQuirks: N26 exports carry two dates, Booking Date and Value Date, and YNAB needs one. The preset uses the booking date, the day the transaction hit your account.
The counterparty is in Partner Name (Payee in older exports) and the purpose in Payment Reference; YNAB keeps them apart as Payee and Memo.
Card payments abroad are already converted to EUR, with the original amount and currency in separate columns; only the EUR amount is imported.
Header names and decimal style vary with the export version and language (English or German names, dot or comma); both are recognised.

howToExport: In online banking, open the account's activity and choose Download or Export.

knownQuirks: A .QFX file carries Quicken's bank ID, and Quicken and QuickBooks can use different IDs for the same bank, so pick your bank again for the .QBO file.
The bank's own transaction IDs (FITID) are kept by default, so QuickBooks still recognises transactions it imported earlier from the bank's own files.
Dates are read as the calendar day written in the file and never shifted by the time zone the bank adds after them.
Files declared CHARSET:1252 are read as Windows-1252, and escaped characters such as & are decoded before the .QBO file is written.

howToExport: En el Dashboard de Stripe, abre los reportes de saldo y elige el periodo que vas a cerrar.
Descarga el CSV detallado de cambios de saldo (el detallado, no el resumen).
Deja las columnas por defecto o añade metadatos; el ajuste solo lee lo que necesita QuickBooks. Suelta el archivo aquí.
knownQuirks: Las horas están en UTC (2024-04-11 22:41:55), así que una venta nocturna en Latinoamérica puede caer al día siguiente; el ajuste mantiene la fecha UTC que informa Stripe.
Cada fila tiene gross, fee y net. QuickBooks concilia contra lo que llega a tu saldo de Stripe, así que se usa el neto.
Los pagos a tu banco aparecen como filas negativas (categoría payout): dinero que sale de Stripe y debe conciliarse como transferencia, no como gasto.
Los metadatos personalizados pueden añadir decenas de columnas; ninguna hace falta para la carga de 3 columnas.

howToExport: En Wise, abre el saldo de la divisa que quieres importar y ve a sus extractos.
Elige el periodo y CSV como tipo de archivo; las cuentas de empresa pueden añadir columnas extra, que el ajuste ignora.
Descarga un archivo por cada saldo de divisa y suéltalo aquí.
knownQuirks: Cada fila trae datos de conversión (Exchange From, Exchange To, Exchange Rate) que la carga de 3 columnas de QuickBooks no admite; se eliminan.
La contraparte está en una columna distinta según la dirección: Payee Name en pagos, Payer Name en cobros y Merchant en compras con tarjeta. El ajuste lee la que esté rellena en cada fila.
La Description de Wise («Card transaction of 32.60 EUR issued by…») repite el importe; contraparte más referencia da una descripción más estable, con la original como respaldo.
Cada extracto corresponde a un saldo en una divisa, así que va a una cuenta de QuickBooks en esa misma divisa.
